explanation: In French business culture, gift-giving is acceptable but must be handled with care to avoid appearing as bribery or excessive familiarity. A modest, tasteful gift (e.g., quality chocolates, wine, or a book) is appropriate after a deal is signed or at the end of a meeting, but not during initial encounters. Avoid overly personal or expensive items, as they can create awkwardness or be misconstrued.
local_tip: Present the gift discreetly, without ostentation, and consider a high-quality regional product from your own country as a conversation starter.
regional_note: In Paris and other major business hubs, corporate gift policies may be stricter; in southern France, the approach can be slightly more relaxed.

also_check.note: Gift-giving is an essential ritual in business; presentation and wrapping are as important as the gift itself.
Gifts are often seen as unnecessary or even suspicious in formal business settings; a small token after a successful partnership is acceptable.
Gift-giving is common and appreciated, but avoid alcohol and ensure gifts respect Islamic customs; use the right hand.
